newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEEKEND ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES.

text.p: Matches this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off 1400 GMT Saturday unless stated):
Barnsley v. West Ham United

Barnsley, in the top flight for the first time in their 110-year history, have strengthened their squad with two major signings, 1.5 million poundS capture Georgi Hristov from Partizan Belgrade and Eric Tinkler from Cagliari.

West Ham coach Harry Redknapp has a defensive crisis with captain Julian Dicks (knee) and Richard Hall (toe) out with long term injuries. Georgian defender Kakhaber Tskhadadze is on trial at the London club.
Blackburn Rovers v. Derby County

Coach Roy Hodgson, who joined from Internazionale in the off-season, will see Scotland defender Colin Hendry back in action, just three weeks after an ankle operation. John Filan will make his Blackburn debut in goal as England international Tim Flowers will be out for six weeks with a groin injury.

Derby coach Jim Smith received a boost this week when striker Dean Sturridge ended speculation of his departure by signing a new four-year contract, although he will be out for four weeks after knee surgery. Costa Rican international Paulo Wanchope (knee) is out for two months, while Croatian captain Aljosa Asanovic (hamstring) is doubtful.
Coventry City v. Chelsea

Coventry City will be without striker Noel Whelan, who picked up an ankle injury pre-season, and defender Roland Nilsson (muscle strain). Their absence will see Gary Breen and John Salako drafted in, while Dion Dublin will move up front, having previously played in defence.

Chelsea coach Ruud Gullit could give Nigerian international Celestine Babayaro his debut if he recovers from a slight knee injury, while defender Steve Clarke (groin) is expected to return. Norwegian striker Tore Andre Flo could be added to the squad.
Everton v. Crystal Palace

Everton coach Howard Kendall is without defenders Andy Hinchcliffe (thigh) and Joe Parkinson (knee), so Tony Thomas, a 400,000 pounds signing from first division Tranmere Rovers this week, is added to the squad. Welsh international Gary Speed will have a late fitness test on a calf injury.

Crystal Palace coach Steve Coppell will give Italian Attilio Lombardo and Paul Warhurst their debuts following moves from Juventus and Blackburn respectively. Striker Dougie Freedman starts a two- match suspension.
Leeds United v. Arsenal

Leeds manager George Graham entertains his former club without midfielder Lee Sharpe, who could be out for up to two months after twisting a knee in a pre-season friendly at Nottingham Forest. Striker Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink is set to make his premier league debut following his two million pounds move from Portuguese side Boavista.

Arsene Wenger will be without off-season signing Gilles Grimandi (ankle) and England defenders Martin Keown (shoulder) and Lee Dixon (ankle). Captain Tony Adams starts a two-match suspension. Liberian striker Christopher Wreh, cousin of George Weah, could be on the bench following his move from Monaco on Thursday.
Leicester City v. Villa

League Cup winners Leicester City are still looking to strengthen their side and are set to sign Blackburn striker Graham Fenton for 1.1 million pounds, while Tony Cottee, currently playing in Japan, could also join coach Martin O'Neill's side.

Aston Villa coach Brian Little could play Dwight Yorke, Savo Milosevic and new signing Stan Collymore up front against his former club. Australia goalkeeper Mark Bosnich has a hamstring injury, so Michael Oakes will deputise.
Newcastle United v. Sheffield Wednesday

Newcastle coach Kenny Dalglish is looking for a morale-boosting victory ahead of Wednesday's European Cup Champions' League qualifying home match against Croatia Zagreb, although he will be without defender Darren Peacock (groin) and strikers Alan Shearer and Des Hamilton (both ankle).

Sheffield Wednesday's latest signing Paulo di Canio, a 4.5 million pounds capture from Celtic, is not expected to play as he is not yet match fit. Coach David Pleat will also be without Jon Newsome (ankle) and Lee Briscoe (groin), although striker Andy Booth could return after a knee injury.
Southampton v. Bolton Wanderers

Southampton coach Dave Jones will be without six key players, including captain Matthew Le Tissier (elbow), Claus Lundekvam (shoulder) and Australian international Robbie Slater (stomach). Norwegian international Stig Johansen could make his debut following his 600,000 pounds transfer from Bodo-Glimt on Wednesday.

Bolton, division one champions last season, will be without long-term injury victims Chris Fairclough and Jon Sheridan (both knee), but off-season signings Robbie Elliott and Neil Cox are set to make their debuts.
Wimbledon v. Liverpool

Wimbledon coach Joe Kinnear welcomes back defender Ben Thatcher, who missed most of last season with an ankle injury. But he will be without veterans John Goodman (knee ligaments) and Mick Harford (achilles).
Liverpool will be without England internationals Robbie Fowler (knee) and Jamie Redknapp (ankle), Czech Patrik Berger and Norwegians Bjorn Tore Kvarme (shoulder) and Oyvind Leonhardsen (hamstring).
Tottenham Hotspur v. Manchester United (kick-off 1500 GMT Sunday)

Coach Gerry Francis is still without striker Chris Armstrong (ankle), midfielder Darren Anderton (hamstring) and defender Clive Wilson (knee and toe), although six million pounds recent signing Les Ferdinand is expected to make his debut.

Champions Manchester United will be without Norwegian striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (ankle ligaments), while Teddy Sheringham returns to White Hart Lane for the first time since his 3.5 million pounds off-season move to Old Trafford.
